'''Valery Antonovich Godyak''' (born June 8, 1941 in [[Czernowitz]]) is a Russian-American physicist who specializes in [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]]. As a scientist, he made fundamental contributions to the understanding of [[radio frequency]] (RF) induced discharges in plasmas as well as in associated nonlinear phenomena.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Godyak|first1=Valery A.|last2=Sternberg|first2=Natalia|date=1990|title=Dynamic model of the electrode sheaths in symmetrically driven rf discharges|journal=Physical Review A|volume=42|issue=4|pages=2299–2312|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.42.2299|pmid=9904281|bibcode=1990PhRvA..42.2299G}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kolobov|first1=V.I.|last2=Godyak|first2=V.A.|date=1995|title=Nonlocal electron kinetics in collisional gas discharge plasmas|journal=IEEE Transactions on Plasma Science|volume=23|issue=4|pages=503–531|doi=10.1109/27.467971|bibcode=1995ITPS...23..503K|issn=1939-9375}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lister|first1=G. G.|last2=Lawler|first2=J. E.|last3=Lapatovich|first3=W. P.|last4=Godyak|first4=V. A.|date=2004|title=The physics of discharge lamps|journal=Reviews of Modern Physics|volume=76|issue=2|pages=541–598|doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.76.541|bibcode=2004RvMP...76..541L}}</ref> As an industrial physicist, he developed [[Induction lamp|induction lamps]] such as the Icetron-Endura RF lamp<ref>{{Cite book|last=Zissis|first=A.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YURZDwAAQBAJ&dq=valery+godyak+endura&pg=PA283|title=Light Sources 2004 Proceedings of the 10th International Symposium on the Science and Technology of Light Sources|date=2004|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-1-4822-6917-8|language=en}}</ref> and received honors from companies such as [[Osram Sylvania]] and [[Siemens]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Godyak&first_nm=Valery&year=2004|title=2004 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=2020-02-26}}</ref>

== Early life and career ==
Godyak received his Engineer-Physicist degree from [[Saint Petersburg State Institute of Technology|Leningrad Technical University]] in 1964. In the same year, he became an assistant professor at Ryazan Radiotechnological University. In 1968, he received his Ph.D. in Plasma Physics at the [[Lomonosov University]] in Moscow. He then worked at the Laboratory of Fusion Engineering at the State Institute of Electro-Physical Apparatus in Leningrad, where he was involved in [[Relativistic electron beam|relativistic electron beams]], [[electron optics]] and [[accelerator physics]]. In 1972, he joined Lomonosov University as a group leader for [[Gas discharge|gas discharges]] with [[Radio wave|radio waves]]. 

In 1980, he was dismissed on political grounds and worked in [[auxiliaries]], for example as an elevator [[electrician]] in a Moscow hospital.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ains.rs/clanstvo/ains.web.ino/GODYAK.VALERY.htm|title=ВАЛЕРИЈ ГОДЈАК|website=www.ains.rs|access-date=2020-02-26}}</ref> In 1984, he joined the United States and became a scientist with the [[GTE|GTE Corporation]] (a follower of the [[Bell Telephone Company]]), following the 1993 takeover of the Lamp Party by Osram at [[Osram Sylvania]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11511015.html|title=Godyak, Valery A.|website=history.aip.org|access-date=2020-02-26}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Godyak is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]].<ref name=":0" />

In 2004, he received the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] with [[Noah Hershkowitz]] for "''fundamental contributions to the physics of low temperature plasmas, including radio frequency wave heating, [[Plasma sheath|sheath physics]], potential profiles, [[Plasma diagnostics|diagnostic probes]], and the industrial applications of plasmas".''<ref name=":0" />
